newsitem.title: UK: Sterling/mark sets new highs, no sign of BoE.
newsitem.headline: Sterling/mark sets new highs, no sign of BoE.

text.p: Sterling pushed to a new 57-month high of 2.8475 marks on Thursday, taking its index against a trade-weighed basket of currencies to its highest level since early May with no sign of Bank of England intervention.
"I don't think the Bank is selling up here...And the trade-weighted index has held above 100 points for most of the day," said a one currency trader.

At 1342 GMT, sterling/mark was trading at 2.8435/45, just below new highs of 2.8475 marks, though well up against 2.8382/87 in late Europe. The pound's trade weighted index stood at 100.4, its highest since hitting 100.6 on May 6.
